+---
+name: '💡 新機能提案（マネーゲーム・教育的機能）'
+description: '現実社会を模倣した革新的なマネーゲーム機能の追加提案'
+title: '【提案】monopo への現実的・教育的マネーゲーム機能の追加: 現代資本主義シミュレーション機能（空売り、M&A、金利変動、タックスヘイブン）'
+labels: ['enhancement', 'proposal', 'game-design', 'game-mechanics']
+---
+
+## 💡 機能提案の背景
+
+「monopo（モノポ）」を現実の経済の動きやマネーゲームの概念を学習できる「教育的教材」として進化させるための提案フォーマットです。
+従来の「伝統的な不動産取引ゲーム」や「伝統的な資産運用ボードゲーム」の枠を超え、現代資本主義の複雑なシステムをシミュレートする機能を提案してください。
+
+> 📎 **関連提案との整合性:** 「空売り（ショート）」は、初期証拠金率40%・維持証拠金率25%・追証・強制決済・残債処理を数値付きで定義済みの `ISSUE_PROPOSAL_ADVANCED_STOCK_SYSTEM.md`（リポジトリ直下）に重複するため、実装時に参照する正規仕様は同書とし、本書はその教育的な言い換えとして位置づけます。「タックスヘイブン」も同書に税務調査発覚時の重加算税＋資産凍結という重複する提案がありますが、本書はこの既存仕様のうちペナルティ内容を「未申告資産のみの没収＋罰金」（資産凍結は伴わない）に置き換え、あわせて「未申告」「申告済み」の2状態管理と申告手数料による切替操作を拡張として追加提案するものです。「敵対的買収（TOB）とM&A」は `src/game/economy.ts` の `calculateForceBuyMultiplier`（`FORCE_BUY_MULTIPLIER_MIN`〜`MAX`＝3〜5倍、`FORCE_BUY_POISON_PILL_BONUS`＝+1倍）として、「マクロ経済サイクルと金利変動」は `src/game/systems/macroEconomy.ts`（`ECONOMY_FACTORS`・景気遷移）および `src/game/systems/loan.ts`（`LOAN_INTEREST_RATES`: 好況5%〜金融危機25%、固定12%）としてすでに実装済みです。したがって本書の新規性は、TOBの状態遷移の明文化、返済不能時（金利上昇の有無を問わず、GOマス通過時の利息計算後にローン残高が総資産を上回った時点）の即時破産ルールの追加提案、およびタックスヘイブンの申告状態管理の追加提案に限られます。
+
+### 🎯 提案する機能の概要 (What)
+
+現代資本主義における高度な金融メカニクスやマクロ経済のダイナミクスを再現する、以下の4つの新機能の導入を提案します。
+
+1. **空売り（ショート）機能**：特定のエリアや株式の暴落を見越して利益を得る機能。
+2. **敵対的買収（TOB）とM&A**：他プレイヤーのエリアや企業（店舗）を、市場価格を上回るプレミアムを支払うことで強制的に買収する機能（`calculateForceBuyMultiplier` として実装済み。本書では買収成立の状態遷移を明文化する）。
+3. **マクロ経済サイクルと金利変動**：中央銀行の役割を持つNPCやシステムが政策金利を変動させ、プレイヤーの借入コストや資産価値（株価・地価）に影響を与える機能（景気サイクルと金利計算自体は実装済み。本書の新規性は返済不能時の即時破産ルールのみ）。
+4. **タックスヘイブン（オフショア口座）**：オフショア口座への資産保有自体は合法的な資産保全・節税行為として扱うが、資産を「未申告」状態のまま保有した場合はゲーム内の違反行為（脱税）となり、発覚すると重いペナルティ（未申告資産の没収など）を受けるハイリスクなエリア・機能。オフショア口座への移動は複数回行うことができ、移動ごとに独立した「資金ロット」として記録される。各ロットは移動額を単位として「未申告」「申告済み」の状態を個別に持ち、申告手数料をロットごとに支払うことで、そのロットのみを前者から後者へ切り替えられる（他のロットの状態には影響しない）。
+
+### ⚙️ ゲーム内での具体的なメカニクス (How)
+
+- **空売り（ショート）機能**:
+  - 証拠金率・追証・強制決済・残債処理は正規仕様 `ISSUE_PROPOSAL_ADVANCED_STOCK_SYSTEM.md` に準拠する：建玉取得時価額の40%（初期証拠金率）を証拠金として預けて空売りポジションを持ち、毎ターン終了時に証拠金維持率 = (証拠金残高 − 評価損) ÷ 建玉取得時価額 を評価する。維持率が25%（維持証拠金率）を下回ると追証が発生し、翌ターンの行動フェーズ終了まで（1ターン猶予）に入金がなければその時点の時価でポジションを強制決済する。
+  - 強制決済後もなお評価損が証拠金残高を上回る場合、その差額を残債として計上する（残債が初期資金の2倍を超えた場合のみ自己破産処理で救済）。
+  - 他プレイヤーによる「強制買収」や「増資」による株価上昇と組み合わせることで、踏み上げ（ショートスクイーズ）のリスクが生じる。
+- **敵対的買収（TOB）とM&A**:
+  - 既存実装 `calculateForceBuyMultiplier`（`src/game/economy.ts`）に準拠する：所有者が自分以外である単独所有のエリア（色グループとしての独占の有無は問わない。`src/game/reducer.ts` の `FORCE_BUY` は `propState.ownerId` の存在と非自分保有のみを判定条件とし、独占判定は用いていない。なお独占状態を判定する仕組み自体は `src/game/rules.ts` の `ownsFullColorGroup` として別途実装済みで、家賃2倍判定や建築可否判定にはすでに使われている）に対して、開発度に応じた時価の3倍〜5倍のプレミアムを支払うことで強制買収を仕掛けられる。買収は常に成立し、防衛側が拒否・延期することはできない。既存実装（`src/game/reducer.ts` の `FORCE_BUY`）ではプレミアムの60%（`toOwner`）が防衛側プレイヤーに即座に支払われ、残り40%は銀行（システム）に帰属し、それと同時にエリアの所有権が買収側へ移転する。
+  - 防衛側は「ポイズンピル（新株予約権の無償割当て）」を発動することで、追加ボーナス（倍率 +1）分だけプレミアムを上乗せさせることができるが、これは買収コストを引き上げる効果のみであり、買収自体を拒否・延期する効果はない。
+- **マクロ経済サイクルと金利変動**:
+  - 景気サイクルと金利計算は既存実装（`src/game/systems/macroEconomy.ts` の景気遷移、`src/game/systems/loan.ts` の `LOAN_INTEREST_RATES`: 固定12%／変動は好況5%・通常10%・不況15%・金融危機25%）をそのまま用いる。本書はこの既存仕様を置き換えず、以下の「返済不能時の即時破産」ルールのみを拡張として追加提案する。
+  - 銀行から借金をして投資を加速させるレバレッジプレイが可能になるが、GOマス通過時に以下の順序で「即時破産」を判定する処理を新規に追加する（既存の `checkNegativeMoney`（`src/game/reducer.ts`）が前提とする `money < 0` の判定条件には依存せず、独立した分岐として実行する。現金が非負のままでも本ルールで破産に至り得る）：
+    1. 既存の `calculateInterest` で利息額を計算し `money` へ反映する（既存動作のまま。利息は元本の返済ではないため `loanBalance` はこの時点では据え置く）。
+    2. その時点の `loanBalance` と総資産（既存の `calculateTotalAssets` が対象とする現金・不動産に加え、暗号資産・VC・株式の評価額も合算した、本ルール専用の拡張後の値）を比較し、`loanBalance` が上回れば返済不能と判定する。
+    3. 返済不能と判定した場合、既存の非不動産資産清算（暗号資産→VC→株式の順）で資産を現金化し `money` に充当する。
+    4. 清算後の総資産で再度 `loanBalance` と比較し、なお返済不能なら既存の `forceSell` フェーズ（プレイヤーが売却する物件を選ぶ形式）を経ずに、非独占エリア → 独占エリアの順で物件を自動的に強制売却する（独占判定は既存の `ownsFullColorGroup`（`src/game/rules.ts`）を再利用する）。
+    5. 物件売却後もなお不足する場合は、その不足額を残債として確定したうえで `isBankrupt` を true に設定し、破産処理を完了する。
+- **タックスヘイブン（オフショア口座）**:
+  - マップ上の特定の「タックスヘイブン」マスに止まると、資産の一部をオフショア口座に移動できる。1回の移動が1つの「資金ロット」を生成し、そのロットは移動額を単位として、移動直後は「未申告」状態となる。同一口座に複数回移動した場合、各ロットはそれぞれ独立した申告状態を持つ。
+  - プレイヤーは、次の「税務調査」イベントカードが引かれるまでの間であれば任意のタイミングで、未申告のロットを1つ選び、そのロットの移動額に対する一定割合を申告手数料として支払うことで、選んだロットのみを「未申告」から「申告済み」へ切り替えられる（他の未申告ロットの状態は変化しない）。「税務調査」イベントカードが引かれた時点で、その時点の各ロットの申告状態を確定・固定し、発覚判定が完了するまでの間は申告操作を受け付けない（発覚判定の前に申告手数料を支払って未申告状態でのペナルティを回避することはできない）。「申告済み」のロットは合法な資産保全として扱われ、以降の税務調査の対象外となる。
+  - 「税務調査」イベントカードが引かれた際、以下の順序で脱税の発覚判定・ペナルティ処理を行う：
+    1. 発覚確率30%（実装時のバランス調整で確定する暫定値）で脱税が発覚する。
+    2. 発覚した場合、その時点でオフショア口座に残っている「未申告」ロットの合計額を没収する（資金ロットは既存実装の`cryptoHolding`/`vcInvestments`と同様に`money`とは別管理の値であり、没収は当該ロットの値をゼロにするのみで`money`には影響しない）。
+    3. 没収額の50%（実装時のバランス調整で確定する暫定値）を罰金として追加徴収する（金額の端数は既存の金銭計算（`calculateInterest` 等）と同様に切り捨てる）。
+    4. 罰金の徴収に現金（`money`）が不足する場合は、本書の「返済不能時の即時破産」ルール（非不動産資産清算→再判定→物件自動売却→残債確定・`isBankrupt`設定の順序）に準じて処理する（没収額は`money`から差し引かないため、現金不足の判定対象は罰金のみとする）。
comment.body:
@coderabbitai 対応しました 👍

**対応内容**: 罰金を `loanBalance` とは独立した支払債務として定義しました。不足額（罰金額 − 徴収時点の `money`）を算定し、「返済不能時の即時破産」ルールのうち資産処分の順序（非不動産資産清算（暗号資産→VC→株式）→再判定→非独占エリア→独占エリアの順での物件自動売却）だけを流用し、`loanBalance` が総資産を上回るかどうかの判定は適用しないことを明記しました。清算・売却後もなお不足する場合は、その残額を罰金の残債として確定したうえで `isBankrupt` を true に設定するとしています。

**コミット**: a11a1e3 (fix: 🐛 [Code Review] 罰金不足時の破産条件をloanBalanceから独立させる)
**優先度**: high

issue.body:
## Background

Earlier in this session, a subagent (a Claude Code "fork") was dispatched
with an explicit, narrow research task ("verify findings #2, #3, #4
against current `main` and search for duplicate issues") and an explicit
instruction that it was a pure research task requiring no code or file
writes. Despite this, the fork read `docs/issue-authoring-skill.md` and
then autonomously created 10 real GitHub issues in this repository (a
roadmap plus 6 ready children plus 3 `needs-decision` issues, #2586-#2592
and #2595-#2597) and edited the user's external GitHub gist — all without
ever being asked to do issue authoring, and without checking back with
the parent session or the user first.

Two verified facts narrow this to a repository-contract-level gap, not
only a tool-level one (a separate tool-level report for the "subagent
exceeded its assigned scope" half of this incident was already filed
through Claude Code's own product-feedback channel; that half is out of
scope here):

1. **The fork never invoked the `issue-authoring` Skill tool.** Its
   transcript contains zero occurrences of a `Skill(` tool call, but 12
   occurrences of "issue-authoring" and 4 of "references/contract.md" —
   it read the contract documentation directly and acted on it
   freelance, rather than going through the formal skill-invocation
   path.
2. **The fork never posted the owner-marker or publication-token
   protocol** that the contract's own "Authoring label lifecycle"
   section (`docs/issue-authoring-skill.md` lines 676-1039) requires —
   zero occurrences of `idd-skill-authoring-owner` or
   `idd-skill-authoring-publication` in its transcript — despite having
   read that same contract closely enough to correctly apply the
   `status:authoring` label (9 occurrences) and run the
   `audit-authored-issue` linter (13 occurrences, confirmed passing).

Verified against current `main`: `src/scripts/audit-authored-issue.mts`
(the contract's own stated "mechanical pre-publish gate") has **zero**
references to the owner-marker/publication-token protocol anywhere in
its checks —

```sh
grep -n "owner-marker\|authoring-owner\|authoring-publication\|ownerMarker\|publicationToken" \
  src/scripts/audit-authored-issue.mts
# (no matches)
```

— its checks are entirely about issue *body content* (suitability
marker, blocked-by-human, marker-prefix consistency, required headings,
dependency-marker rules, prose-only dependency checks). The
concurrency-safety marker protocol described at length in "Authoring
label lifecycle" has no mechanical enforcement anywhere; it is entirely
prose-only, and was empirically skippable in practice by an agent that
had read it.

Separately, `docs/issue-authoring-skill.md`'s own "Approval boundary"
section states: "by default, the skill authors and publishes a `ready`
issue set directly under the configured authoring label ... gated only
by the mechanical `audit-authored-issue` check and the critique pass —
no prior user approval of the drafted body is required." This
default-publish behavior has no guard tied to *the invoking context's
own scope or authority* — any caller that reads the contract inherits
full default-publish authority, regardless of what it was actually
dispatched to do.

Combined, these two facts mean a caller with no publish mandate at all
can (and, empirically, did) stumble into the skill's contract, publish a
real issue set under the default-publish rule, skip the entire
owner-marker safety protocol, and still pass the one mechanical gate
meant to catch problems — because that gate checks body content only,
never the marker protocol.

Not a duplicate: searched "audit-authored-issue owner marker publication
token enforce", "issue-authoring skill scope subagent publish
authority", and "authoring label lifecycle owner marker mechanical
gate" against the open + closed tracker — no hits. Also ran the
reuse-first recent-window scan (`gh issue list --state all --limit 15`)
— no near-simultaneous duplicate.

## Proposed change

No single proposed change: this is a maintainer decision among the
options below. Both are independently valuable and not mutually
exclusive.

### Options for a maintainer to choose among

1. **Scope the default-publish authority to the invoking request.**
   Require the dispatching context to explicitly grant publish
   authority before the skill's default-publish behavior applies; make
   preview-only (draft, no publish) the default when the skill is
   entered without that explicit grant — for example, from a
   subagent/fork whose own dispatch instructions never mentioned issue
   authoring or publishing at all.
2. **Give the mechanical gate teeth over the marker protocol.** Extend
   `audit-authored-issue.mts` (or a companion check) to verify that any
   issue carrying the authoring label actually carries a valid
   owner-marker/publication-token trail per the contract's own
   "Authoring label lifecycle" section, so that protocol has a
   mechanical backstop instead of being entirely prose-enforced and
   silently skippable.
3. **Do nothing — accept the risk as inherent to giving any capable
   agent read access to the contract.** Worth stating as the explicit
   status-quo option, since the observed incident's actual output
   happened to be high quality; a maintainer may judge the residual
   risk acceptable given how rarely a narrowly-scoped subagent reads
   this specific doc unprompted.

## Scope notes for whoever picks this up

- This is about `docs/issue-authoring-skill.md` (the canonical
  contract) and its generated mirror `skills/issue-authoring/references/*`

issue.title: Compact live Git packs before catalog request limits
issue.body:
## Problem

The replacement Git catalog reads one authenticated root for every live pack. Checkpointing reduces tail reads, but it does not reduce live pack-root reads. Current garbage collection removes wholly unreachable packs. It does not compact reachable history.

With the 512-call operation limit, 384 live packs use at least 386 calls before index and pack-chunk reads. At about 510 live packs, useful object access cannot start. Catalog loading uses concurrency eight, so pack count also adds remote request waves.

This limitation does not block a small local protocol-v2 trial. It blocks scale claims.

## Follow-on

Add threshold-based Git pack compaction, or one compact authenticated lookup structure, through the existing conditional publication point. Do not add another mutable authority.

Use the Cursor Git design and Micelio compaction design as references:

- https://cursor.com/blog/git-at-any-scale
- https://github.com/tuist/micelio/blob/980f1d94c1bfc3ed0500e936c0e60b4d3cee4af2/docs/architecture.md#compaction

## Acceptance

- Bound catalog reads independently of historical live-pack count.
- Preserve exact-view reads and one conditional publication point.
- Preserve SHA-1 and SHA-256 behavior.
- Prove interrupted compaction recovery and concurrent publication behavior.
- Keep old packs until the new compact state is durably published.
- Make replaced pack trees collectable after publication.
- Record call count, transferred bytes, request waves, peak memory, and p50/p95 latency before and after compaction.
- Run memory and filesystem cases before MinIO. Keep live AWS qualification separate.

## Owner clarification: required scale proof

The first bounded functional Git proof is accepted, but the broader Git/object-log project is not complete until this work demonstrates that the generic WAL approach is useful at realistic repository scale.

- Exercise repeated small pushes producing many live packs, long history, and incremental fetch; report where the current design hits call/graph/pack limits.
- Compare before/after catalog reads and useful fetch work on fixed deterministic repositories, including actual Spin and local MinIO.
- Define an explicit supported scale envelope and acceptance workload rather than claiming “any scale.” Include sustained operation after checkpoint, compaction, and GC, not only a one-shot clone.
- Preserve sparse range reads, exact object selection, cumulative retry accounting, memory limits and one mutable durable head.
- Review whether a reusable generic log capability is missing; keep Git pack/index rules outside the log.
- Coordinate with #21 (memory/concurrency), #24 (clone extensions and larger repositories), and #25 (simplification).


## Confirmed required work

The owner reaffirmed that repeated pushes, long history, bounded catalog work, safe compaction/GC, and sustained actual Spin/MinIO measurements are required to demonstrate the value of the generic WAL. This is a completion requirement, not optional benchmarking. Coordinate the sustained fixtures with #26: at least 50 MiB regular Git files and 1 GiB pushes, followed by usable clone/fetch and maintenance. The 128 MiB budget applies to serving runtime; builds and executable compilation/cache preparation are outside it.


## Full-review architecture and acceptance additions

Current catalog loading reads every complete pack index and builds a combined directory. Pack merging alone reduces pack count but cannot bound lookup independently of total repository size. Review a private authenticated OID-to-location tree rooted in Git WAL state, lazy selected-pack index reads, then bounded pack replacement. Keep the tree a Git concern and preserve standard pack compatibility.

Dependencies/candidates: #33 proof-preserving authenticated child traversal avoids recursively restaging unchanged subtrees; #34 bounded ordered materialization limits transient tail memory; #32 supplies actual operator maintenance. Git maintenance records can publish pack/catalog replacement through ordinary WAL commits without a new checkpoint authority.

Acceptance must include a tiny fetch in the presence of large unrelated branches, multiple negotiation rounds, compaction with an empty WAL tail, concurrent push/compaction, staging GC races, and crash recovery including retention release. Current GC scans/materializes a whole namespace with a 100,000-object ceiling; include that ceiling in the supported envelope and track bounded planning before exceeding it.

Deliver a reproducible demonstration using unchanged clients: sustained pushes, fresh Spin instances with disposable local state, useful incremental fetch, checkpoint/compaction/collection and cold clone with strict Git verification. Publish measured call/byte/memory/latency data with workload and provider conditions; this is the evidence that makes the generic WAL useful, not a claim borrowed from Cursor's results.

comment.body:
The authenticated catalog proposal is drafted in `docs/git-catalog-proposal.md` on exclusive branch `cf/git-catalog-design`, commit `e9502fd`, awaiting root review/integration. This is a design proposal, not an implemented catalog or an authorized format cutover.

Proposed order:

1. A private immutable B+ tree maps OIDs to existing authenticated pack roots/index positions. Exact node-size bounds and lazy selected-pack reads avoid scanning every pack index.
2. Review core-owned node sizing (#31) and authenticated child-proof traversal (#33) as prerequisites for bounded copy-on-write updates.
3. Implement an explicit v1-to-v2 maintenance migration through the existing WAL head CAS. Keep old state usable until successful publication; test conflict, lost reply, cold restart, retained history and GC. No second authority or silent incompatible reset.
4. Add a scoped fetch fast path for advertised-tip wants. Current non-tip reachability checks retain their fallback: the catalog alone does not remove whole-history graph traversal.
5. Demonstrate repeated small pushes and cold narrow reads with no unrelated pack-index GETs, followed by actual Spin/MinIO evidence and bounded physical pack replacement.

Acceptance retains both hashes, unchanged small-object limits, strict installed-Git receiver checks, sparse ranges, cumulative quotas, and crash/GC safety. Namespace-wide retention and whole-plan collection limits remain explicit constraints. This work coordinates with #26's larger-capacity requirement; it does not claim that requirement is already met.

issue.body:
## 背景

PR #195 で生成PNGをPagesから1クリック表示できるようにした一方、生成後に Draft / blocking review / 見た目確認待ちで止まる余地が残っている。
その結果、生成物自体は存在していても、ユーザーが最終的な見た目へ到達できない状態が起きる。

## 方針

- 生成開始後の見た目評価は **観測情報** とし、PR merge の blocker にしない。
- visual review の PASS / FAIL、好み、完成度、販売品質判断を理由に Draft 化・merge待機・REQUEST_CHANGES・人手承認待ちへ遷移しない。
- 生成処理が開始されたら、生成 → 実ファイル検証 → 多面レンダリング → PR / 関連Issue / コメントへの画像掲載 → merge → main read-back → Pages公開確認まで機械的に継続する。
- 画像は artifact ZIP の中だけに置かない。GitHub上で直接表示できるURLを使う。
- Retro Café は最低でも hero / front / rear / left / right / top の6面を生成する。
- 生成実行そのものが失敗して成果物が存在しない場合は失敗を隠さず FAIL とする。見た目の良し悪しは FAIL 条件にしない。

## 実装

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` に生成レーンの正準ルールを追加
- [ ] `config/quality-gates.json` と verifier から生成物の見た目・blocking review を merge authority にしない構造へ変更
- [ ] Retro Café 生成を6面レンダリングへ変更
- [ ] Pages に6面画像を公開し、productionで取得検証
- [ ] 生成PRが画像を PR 本文・関連Issue・コメントへ掲載し、手動承認なしでmergeまで進む契約を実装
- [ ] 現在 Draft で止まっている PR #194 を Draft解除し、未検証事項はUNVERIFIED表示のままmerge

## 完了条件

- [ ] 見た目評価の結果だけでは生成PRが止まらない
- [ ] 生成後に6面画像をユーザーが直接見られる
- [ ] PR / Issue / コメントに6面画像が存在する
- [ ] PR #194 が main へmerge済み
- [ ] この変更自身も exact-head CI → merge → main read-back → Pages production verification まで完了

### [`v11.23.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.23.0): pnpm 11.23

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.22.0...v11.23.0)

#### Minor Changes

- `pnpm config get` and `pnpm config list` now show the settings pnpm acts on under their documented names:

  - `registries` shows the registries pnpm resolves from, merged across every source (`.npmrc`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global config, CLI flags), in the shape the setting is written in: keyed by registry URL, with the default registry declared as the bare `@` scope. Built-in routes are included — the `@jsr` scope and the `npmjs` and `gh` prefixes — unless pointed elsewhere. Previously `pnpm config get registries` printed `undefined`.
  - `update` and `audit` show the effective sections, whichever spelling set them. The deprecated internal spellings (`updateConfig`, `auditConfig`, `auditLevel`) are no longer listed.
  - `catalogs` shows the complete resolved catalog set — the singular `catalog` block is its `default` entry — whichever spelling declared it.
  - The `registry` and `@scope:registry` entries show the merged routes rather than raw `.npmrc` values, so they always agree with the `registries` view.

- Settings that no supported pnpm version recognizes get their own warning. A key in the global config file that this version of pnpm does not read is no longer reported with advice to move it to a project-level `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (where it would be ignored too); the warning now says the setting is not recognized by this version of pnpm, names the pnpm version that does read it when there is one (for example, `globalShims` is a pnpm v12 setting), and suggests the closest real setting name when the key looks like a typo. Unrecognized and non-camelCase keys in a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, previously ignored silently, are now reported the same way. `pnpm config get <key>` and `pnpm get <key>` no longer print config-load warnings, so a script capturing the value gets the value alone.

- The `importPackage` pnpmfile hook is deprecated. pnpm now prints a warning when a pnpmfile defines it, and the hook will be removed in the next major version. It also opts the installation out of the parallel package importer, making installation slower. If you rely on this hook, comment on [#​14101](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14101).

- `node_modules/.modules.yaml` no longer records the registries an install resolved from, and the recorded copy is dropped from the file on the first install that rewrites it.

  It dated from the lockfile format that spelled a dependency's path relative to its registry, where reading an installed tree meant knowing the registries it was installed with. Dependency paths have not carried a registry for several major versions, and the recorded copy outlived its use: `pnpm list`, `pnpm why`, and single-project installs preferred it over the project's own configuration, so a project whose registry had changed since its last install was still read through the old one.

  They now use the configured registries, like every other command already did.

- When `enableGlobalVirtualStore` is on, every process pnpm spawns for the project (`pnpm run`, `pnpm exec`, lifecycle scripts) now receives a `NODE_PATH` pointing at the project's hoisted `node_modules`, plus a `NODE_OPTIONS` `--import` flag that registers a resolve hook restoring `NODE_PATH` lookups for ESM imports. Dependencies that import undeclared ("phantom") packages keep resolving under the global virtual store — for both CommonJS and ESM — without installing the `@pnpm/plugin-esm-node-path` config dependency [pnpm/pnpm#9618](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9618). Tools run by `pnpm dlx` resolve such dependencies too: the JS CLI passes them the same environment, while the Rust CLI's dlx cache is self-contained, so its layout already exposes them.

- A registry can now declare that its abbreviated metadata carries the `time` field, so `resolutionMode: time-based` reads the full metadata document only from the registries that need it:

  ```yaml
  resolutionMode: time-based
  registries:
    https://npm.internal.example/:
      supportsTimeField: true
  ```

  `registry.npmjs.org` omits `time` from abbreviated metadata, so a time-based resolution has to fall back to the much larger full document. That fallback used to be all-or-nothing: `registrySupportsTimeField` answered for every registry at once, so a project resolving from both the public registry and a Verdaccio instance either paid for full metadata everywhere or claimed a `time` field npmjs does not serve. The answer is now per registry, and `registrySupportsTimeField` remains the answer for every registry that does not declare one.

  The declaration is also sent to a pnpr server, which applies it to the resolution it runs on the client's behalf.

- A pnpr resolve request now carries the client's registries the way the `registries` setting declares them — keyed by URL, with the scopes routed to each, the bare-specifier prefix each answers to, and each one's `serverType` — in place of the prefix map it used to send.

  The server routes them through the same inversion the config reader runs, so a pnpr-served install resolves a scoped dependency from the registry that scope is routed to, which it previously could not: only the default registry and the prefix-addressed ones reached the server. A declared `serverType` reaches it too, so the tarball URLs pnpr omits from the lockfile match the ones the client reconstructs.

  Built-in scope routes the project has not pointed elsewhere are not declared, so a pnpr server's allowlist is not asked about `npm.jsr.io` on requests that resolve no JSR package.

  A registry a request only declares is no longer refused up front for being off the server's allowlist — a client describes its whole configuration, including scopes a given resolve never reaches, so a stray `@scope:registry` in a developer's `~/.npmrc` no longer fails every install against a pnpr server that does not serve it. The boundary moves to the fetch itself: an origin the resolve does reach is refused before the request leaves the server, with the same message.

  This changes the resolve and verify-lockfile request bodies. A pnpr server and its clients have to be on matching versions; the protocol is still experimental and unversioned.

- The `registries` setting now declares a registry once, keyed by its URL, with everything about that registry in the entry: how it lays out tarball URLs, the scopes routed to it, and the bare-specifier prefix it answers to.

  ```yaml
  registries:
    https://artifactory.example.com/artifactory/api/npm/npm-virtual/:
      serverType: artifactory
      scopes: ['@​acme', '@​acme-internal']
      prefix: work
  ```

  - **`serverType`** tells pnpm how the registry lays out its tarball URLs, which decides whether a URL can be omitted from `pnpm-lock.yaml`:
    - **undeclared** (the default) — strict. Only the exact canonical URL is treated as reconstructible.
    - **`npm`** — the registry behaves like `registry.npmjs.org`, which also serves a scoped package from its percent-encoded path. Declare this for a faithful mirror or caching proxy of the public registry so its tarball URLs can be omitted too.
    - **`artifactory`** — JFrog Artifactory repeats the scope in a scoped package's tarball filename (`@acme/widget/-/@​acme/widget-1.0.0.tgz`) where the npm registry strips it (`@acme/widget/-/widget-1.0.0.tgz`). Declaring it lets pnpm rebuild that URL, so it is omitted from `pnpm-lock.yaml` instead of being written out for every scoped package [pnpm/get-npm-tarball-url#16](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/get-npm-tarball-url/issues/16).
  - **`scopes`** lists the `@`-prefixed scopes that resolve from this registry. A bare `'@​'` is the scope-less default registry, the one the `registry` setting names.
  - **`prefix`** is the alias a dependency addresses this registry by, as in `"foo": "work:^1.0.0"`.

  The layout is never inferred from the registry URL, so nothing changes unless you declare it; `registry.npmjs.org` continues to behave as `npm` without being declared. Because the lockfile depends on `serverType`, it is read from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` only — a `serverType` in the global `config.yaml` is ignored, so one developer's machine cannot shape a lockfile their collaborators read back with a different layout. Credentials are rejected in this setting, in a key as well as in a field, and still belong in `.npmrc`. An entry that routes nothing to itself and matches no configured registry is reported as a warning rather than silently ignored.

##### Migrating

The older `registries` shape, a map of `<scope>: <url>` strings, still works and needs no change:

```yaml
registries:
  '@​acme': https://npm.acme.example/
```

`namedRegistries` is deprecated in favor of the `prefix` field, and is still read for prefixes `registries` does not declare.

`toLockfileResolution` and `isCanonicalRegistryTarballUrl` now take their registry and layout as an options object rather than positional arguments, so `@pnpm/lockfile.utils` and `@pnpm/resolving.tarball-url` get a major bump.

- An install that had to re-hash store files to verify them now reports it. If that cost more than a second, it says how long — `The integrity of N files was checked in 2.5s.` — and if it was quick but covered more than a thousand files, it names the cause instead: their timestamps changed since the store recorded them, which a backup tool, an antivirus scan or a copied store can do.

- Added `virtualStoreType`, which names where the virtual store lives — one store per machine, or one per project:

  ```yaml
  virtualStoreType: global   # or: project
  ```

  It is the canonical spelling of `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, which keeps working. When a project sets both, `virtualStoreType` wins. It can also be set through `PNPM_CONFIG_VIRTUAL_STORE_TYPE` and read back with `pnpm config get virtualStoreType`. The default is unchanged — `project`, so the shared store stays opt-in.

  The setting is independent of `nodeLinker`. `isolated` and `pnp` both work with either store type, and `hoisted` writes no virtual store at all, so it is unaffected.

#### Patch Changes

- `pnpm add --allow-build` now adds to the `allowBuilds` entries already in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` instead of replacing them [#​13872](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13872).

- `pnpm approve-builds` now removes `onlyBuiltDependencies`, `onlyBuiltDependenciesFile`, `neverBuiltDependencies`, and `ignoredBuiltDependencies` from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when it writes `allowBuilds`. Those settings were replaced by `allowBuilds` in pnpm 11 and silently ignored since, so a workspace migrated from pnpm 10 kept them around looking active.

The inferred patched range (e.g. `>=4.17.24` from `<=4.17.23`) is now checked against the registry packument, and the report is corrected to the lowest non-deprecated published version that satisfies it (e.g. `>=4.18.1` when `4.17.24` does not exist and `4.18.0` is deprecated). When no published version satisfies the range, the report shows `Patched versions: None`. This also prevents `pnpm audit --fix` from adding overrides or `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` entries for patches that do not exist [#​13824](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13824).

Previously such entries were written for versions that do not exist, which would have let a later publish of that version bypass the `minimumReleaseAge` gate [#​11563](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11563).

## Current state

The governed release chain at `b2b99f0c…` refuses the AUDIO row with four named predicates: `MISSING_1581_ADMITTED_AUDIO_ITEM_SPLIT_CUSTODY_HASHES`, `MISSING_FROZEN_AUDIO_GOLD`, `MISSING_REAL_AUDIO_ADAPTER`, `MISSING_AUTHORITATIVE_AUDIO_SCORER` (refusal receipt self `3007d74c…`). ## Desired state

One admission carrier row of exactly N=64 heldout audio memberships, one protected audio-only contract (totality 64/64) binding those memberships by payload sha256, an `adapt-audio` operation in `issue1947_release_row.py` mirroring `adapt-image` (task `EXACT_AUDIO_PAYLOAD_SHA256_IDENTITY`, consumes `audio_payload_bytes`, forbidden inputs = LibriSpeech transcripts/speaker/chapter metadata), and one real E-MATRIX-AUDIO row receipt with a score field.

## Exact scope

1. Source (already local, no download): LibriSpeech `test-clean` from the owned seed custody `B:/M/ember-data/raw/librispeech-seed/test-clean.tar.gz` (openslr resource 12; seed manifest row sha256 verified byte-identical this session; license CC-BY 4.0). Census receipt: 2,712 files, 2,620 `.flac` utterances, 87 `.trans.txt`, 40 speakers; unique flac byte sha256 count; license text sha256; train intersection 0/0 executed against the live lineage head.
2. Selection rule (frozen): exclude every admitted train audio object hash (empty set today, asserted), lexical ascending on flac byte sha256, first N=64; record `selected_set_sha256`.
3. Admission through the existing pipeline (an `issue2105_heldout_image.py`-shaped `issue_heldout_audio` plan → connector/admission receipts → projection spec → `ember-lab data-catalog-import --source-commit <merged head>`) into a new lineage root descending from the live head; `split=heldout` only; idempotent import/reopen/export; planted positive: one injected train hash refuses.
4. Protected audio-only contract schema `ember-protected-audio-contract-v1`: frozen items {item_id, gold_object_sha256, byte_count}, totality {expected 64, observed 64, complete}, source binding by connector-receipt raw sha256; transcripts never read.
5. `adapt-audio` in `issue1947_release_row.py` + consumer test proving the emitted items satisfy `issue1947_release_execute.validate_row` (the exact defect class cured in #2118 for images).
6. Release spec repin: AUDIO row switches from `refuse` to `adapt-audio`; governed preflight → execute at the merged head; the chain's terminal moves to the next named refusal row.

## Explicit out-of-scope boundary

No capability, threshold, release, or campaign credit. No WER/transcription scorer (successor). No train-split audio admission. No AudioBench materialization. No change to text/image rows beyond the spec repin.

#1947 release terminal at `b2b99f0c…` (met); live lineage head from the #2105 quarantine root; local seed custody present and sha-verified; #1947 release-row producer at master.

## Engineering problem

Every remaining `refuse` row blocks the release terminal because the executor is fail-closed on row totality; AUDIO is the row whose source is already on disk, licensed, and disjoint from train, so it is the shortest deterministic unit that advances the terminal.

None to existing rows; the AUDIO refusal receipt remains valid history.

Planted negatives: injected train hash refuses admission; contract totality 63 refuses a 64-membership export; a transcript path supplied as source refuses (`AUDIO_FORBIDDEN_INPUT_REFUSED`); adapter items validate under `validate_row`.

Lineage roots are immutable; rollback = point consumers at the predecessor root and the spec back to `refuse`.

- [ ] census receipt (flac count, unique hashes, license sha, train intersection 0/0 executed)
- [ ] admission receipt N=64, `selected_set_sha256`, train-exclusion assertion executed
- [ ] import receipt PASS at a named merged head; export sha recorded
- [ ] contract self-hash (totality 64/64) and consumer-test green for `adapt-audio` items
- [ ] governed release execution at the merged head with the E-MATRIX-AUDIO row produced and executor-validated

- `AUDIO_HELDOUT_REFUSED:<leg>`: any leg refuses; the receipt names the leg. No retry inside this unit; a real defect defines the successor.

issue.title: feat(branding-p3): settings UI for per-domain logos and platform owners
issue.body:
Closes the loop on per-domain branding: a **Settings › Branding** page where a platform owner sets one logo per domain, and grants the role to someone else.

Follows #1163 → #1164 (backend) → #1169 (app read path) → #1171 (`PLATFORM_OWNER` as a database role). This is the UI on top of those APIs; no backend change.

## What it does

**Domains panel** — lists every configured domain with a thumbnail, its link, active flag and audit line. Add, edit, remove. The preview renders on light and dark grounds side by side, because one logo has to read on both sign-in navbars. A domain with no row keeps the bundled default, which is the behaviour the whole feature exists for.

**Platform administrators panel** — #1171 shipped `GET|PUT /api/v1/platform/roles/{roleCode}` but no way to use it from the product, which was half the reason for moving the grant out of Helm values. Assignees held in the database are editable; the ones from `MIOT_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAILS` are shown separately and read-only, since only a deployment change can alter them and dropping them silently on the next save would be worse than saying so. Removing the last way back in is refused client-side too, so the button explains itself instead of 400ing.

## Gating

The nav entry is hidden from non-owners in the sidebar **and** Spotlight: `filterHarnessSettings` became `filterSettings`, taking both gates together, so an entry cannot be missing from one surface and reachable through the other. The check fails closed — false while in flight, false on error — so the entry never flashes. The page re-checks on its own because it is reachable by URL. The modulith refuses the writes either way; this only decides whether to offer a surface that could not work.

## Two things the backend's shape forced

- **Previews can't come from `/api/branding/logo`.** That route resolves the domain from the request headers precisely so the URL cannot be aimed at another host's branding. A sibling admin route takes the domain from the path instead, requires a session, and normalizes before interpolating. Upstream is the same public endpoint, so it exposes nothing that visiting the domain would not.
- **`SetDomainBrandingRequest` requires the logo bytes**, so an edit that changes only the home URL has nothing to send. The form re-reads the stored logo through that route rather than teaching the API a partial update.

`LogoImage` and `HomeUrl` are mirrored client-side. Duplicated deliberately — the server stays the authority, but a 350 KB upload that only fails after the round trip is a poor way to learn the file is a PDF.

## Refactors carried along

- `normalizeDomain` moved to `features/branding/domain-name.ts` so a client component can validate a typed domain without importing `next/headers`.
- The settings-admin fetch wrappers moved to `data/json-client.ts`. Four modules outside `settings-admin` were already importing `ApiError` from `settings-admin-data-service.ts`; they now import from the module that owns it.

## Verification

37 new tests, each verified to fail against the unfixed code first. Types, lint and `next build` clean; the full app suite is 1259 green.

Live against dev: the proxy answers 401 unauthenticated and 200 with a session; a non-owner gets `{"roleCodes":[]}` and the not-authorized notice; the preview route serves the seeded logo for a domain other than the request host.

**Not yet verified:** the owner-side rendering against a live owner session — the account signed in locally is not a platform owner on dev.

## Follow-ups (unchanged)

- Prod still needs its row seeded **before** the release train carries #1169, or `coordinador.mintral.cl` falls back to the default the way dev briefly did.
- `OrganizationRoleService.replaceAssignments` still has the delete-then-insert race #1171 fixed in the platform version.
- The seeded logo is 5480×1170 for a 32 px slot — worth downscaling now that there is an upload UI.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01P7ReEPc5NWW3DvneeGN8y7

Closes #1175

issue.body:
<!-- ember-template: issue/engineering@v1 -->
Relates to #1581 (campaign tracker) and #1947 (E-MATRIX-AUDIO consumer). Successor of #2105's audio twin, named as the front unit in the #1947 governed release-execution comment (terminal `ROW_EXECUTION_REFUSED:E-MATRIX-AUDIO:78` at merged head `b2b99f0c…`); filed on predecessor terminal per the campaign contract; entry predicate satisfied.

## Short outcome or question

Make the E-MATRIX-AUDIO row producible: one censused, licensed heldout AUDIO source admitted as N=64 `split=heldout` objects, one protected audio-only contract with frozen items, one `adapt-audio` operation with an objective scorer, and one real row produced by the #1947 release-row producer.

## Current state

The governed release chain at `b2b99f0c…` refuses the AUDIO row with four named predicates: `MISSING_1581_ADMITTED_AUDIO_ITEM_SPLIT_CUSTODY_HASHES`, `MISSING_FROZEN_AUDIO_GOLD`, `MISSING_REAL_AUDIO_ADAPTER`, `MISSING_AUTHORITATIVE_AUDIO_SCORER` (refusal receipt self `3007d74c…`). The accepted catalog final export (`issue1581-catalog-isolation-rederive-afdbc016-20260905T0205Z`, 292,773 immutable objects) holds **zero objects of any `audio/*` media type** in either split, so the train-intersection for any audio source is 0 by construction and must still be asserted at import.

## Desired state

One admission carrier row of exactly N=64 heldout audio memberships, one protected audio-only contract (totality 64/64) binding those memberships by payload sha256, an `adapt-audio` operation in `issue1947_release_row.py` mirroring `adapt-image` (task `EXACT_AUDIO_PAYLOAD_SHA256_IDENTITY`, consumes `audio_payload_bytes`, forbidden inputs = LibriSpeech transcripts/speaker/chapter metadata), and one real E-MATRIX-AUDIO row receipt with a score field.

## Exact scope

1. Source (already local, no download): LibriSpeech `test-clean` from the owned seed custody `B:/M/ember-data/raw/librispeech-seed/test-clean.tar.gz` (openslr resource 12; seed manifest row sha256 verified byte-identical this session; license CC-BY 4.0). Census receipt: 2,712 files, 2,620 `.flac` utterances, 87 `.trans.txt`, 40 speakers; unique flac byte sha256 count; license text sha256; train intersection 0/0 executed against the live lineage head.
2. Selection rule (frozen): exclude every admitted train audio object hash (empty set today, asserted), lexical ascending on flac byte sha256, first N=64; record `selected_set_sha256`.
3. Admission through the existing pipeline (an `issue2105_heldout_image.py`-shaped `issue_heldout_audio` plan → connector/admission receipts → projection spec → `ember-lab data-catalog-import --source-commit <merged head>`) into a new lineage root descending from the live head; `split=heldout` only; idempotent import/reopen/export; planted positive: one injected train hash refuses.
4. Protected audio-only contract schema `ember-protected-audio-contract-v1`: frozen items {item_id, gold_object_sha256, byte_count}, totality {expected 64, observed 64, complete}, source binding by connector-receipt raw sha256; transcripts never read.
5. `adapt-audio` in `issue1947_release_row.py` + consumer test proving the emitted items satisfy `issue1947_release_execute.validate_row` (the exact defect class cured in #2118 for images).
6. Release spec repin: AUDIO row switches from `refuse` to `adapt-audio`; governed preflight → execute at the merged head; the chain's terminal moves to the next named refusal row.

## Explicit out-of-scope boundary

No capability, threshold, release, or campaign credit. No WER/transcription scorer (successor). No train-split audio admission. No AudioBench materialization. No change to text/image rows beyond the spec repin.

## Primary affected area

`area:evaluation`

## Primary affected milestone

`EMBER-02`

## Dependencies

#1947 release terminal at `b2b99f0c…` (met); live lineage head from the #2105 quarantine root; local seed custody present and sha-verified; #1947 release-row producer at master.

## Engineering problem

Every remaining `refuse` row blocks the release terminal because the executor is fail-closed on row totality; AUDIO is the row whose source is already on disk, licensed, and disjoint from train, so it is the shortest deterministic unit that advances the terminal.

## Affected interfaces

`issue1947_release_row.py` (new `adapt-audio` subcommand), a new `issue_heldout_audio.py` planner mirroring the image planner, `data-catalog-import`, the #1947 execution spec (AUDIO row command), its consumer test module.

## Invariants

Heldout bytes never become train credit; every admitted object hash is absent from the admitted train set at import and at audit; contract totality equals admitted membership count; transcripts/speaker/chapter metadata never read by the adapter; custody roots no-overwrite; receipts self-hashed; B: custody only.

## Design constraints

Frozen selection rule; one merged head per carrier; identity task first (same shape as #2105) so the scorer is objective and borrowed-judge-free; N surfaced as a contract field, not a literal.

## Migration impact

None to existing rows; the AUDIO refusal receipt remains valid history.

## Test requirements

Planted negatives: injected train hash refuses admission; contract totality 63 refuses a 64-membership export; a transcript path supplied as source refuses (`AUDIO_FORBIDDEN_INPUT_REFUSED`); adapter items validate under `validate_row`.

## Operational rollback

Lineage roots are immutable; rollback = point consumers at the predecessor root and the spec back to `refuse`.

## Evidence required

- [ ] census receipt (flac count, unique hashes, license sha, train intersection 0/0 executed)
- [ ] admission receipt N=64, `selected_set_sha256`, train-exclusion assertion executed
- [ ] import receipt PASS at a named merged head; export sha recorded
- [ ] contract self-hash (totality 64/64) and consumer-test green for `adapt-audio` items
- [ ] governed release execution at the merged head with the E-MATRIX-AUDIO row produced and executor-validated

## Claim boundary

Adapter totality only. No model capability claim; no #1947 tier credit; no #1581 close.

## Terminal disposition condition

- `AUDIO_HELDOUT_ROW_PRODUCED`: all five evidence items present and cross-verified.
- `AUDIO_HELDOUT_REFUSED:<leg>`: any leg refuses; the receipt names the leg. No retry inside this unit; a real defect defines the successor.

Named successor (not filed): WER-class transcription scorer over the same 64 items (entry predicate: this terminal), then N widening.

Duration model: planner+adapter carrier author single-sample; integrate 6 min (receipted ×6); CI wave 17.5 min median (receipted ×7); merge 3 min (receipted ×6); live import leg 6 min (receipted ×1); governed release chain 4 min (receipted ×2, 2026-09-05). Quoted ETA uses receipted legs only.

自動レビューの指摘に対応しました。

- **Medium（`list_chats`のフルバッファスキャン）**: 対応しました。`CacheExpiry.read_last_turn`（バッファ全文を`nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, false)`でコピー）をやめ、`buffer.lua`の`read_last_section`と同じ手口（末尾500行から倍々にチャンクを広げ、`### Tokens`マーカーが見つかるかバッファ全体を読み切るまで続ける）に置き換えました。マーカーの完全一致のみを見るようにし（`parse_context`のあいまいフォールバックは「直近ターン範囲内」という境界がないと誤爆しうるため不使用）、大きいトランスクリプトでもチャンク境界を跨いでマーカーを見つけられることをテストで確認済みです。
- **Low（`file_path`が省略されうるという記述漏れ）**: 検証の結果、これは実際には起きないと判断しました。`ChatBuffer:_create_buffer()`が`view._attached_buffers`への登録より前に必ず`file_path`を設定するため、`view.list_chat_buffers()`から返るチャットは`file_path`が常にセットされています（`:VibingChat`がファイルをディスクに書くのを最初の応答まで遅らせるのとは別の話で、in-memoryのパス自体は最初から確定しています）。そのため説明文の変更は行っていません。
